name: Syed Nazrul Islam
role: Acting President of the Provisional Government
contribution: As acting president of the Provisional Government of Bangladesh, he preserved constitutional continuity while Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was imprisoned in Pakistan and kept wartime political authority intact.
context: Mujibnagar Government, 1971; amid wartime uncertainty and absent central leadership.
impact: His acting presidency helped present the Liberation War as the struggle of a legitimate national government, not a fragmented rebellion.
highlight: In uncertainty, he became the constitutional voice of continuity.
seoTitle: Syed Nazrul Islam - 1971 Liberation War Profile
seoDescription: Syed Nazrul Islam served as acting president of the Provisional Government of Bangladesh in 1971, preserving constitutional continuity while Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was imprisoned in Pakistan.
shortAnswer: Acting president of the Provisional Government of Bangladesh in 1971 and a key guardian of wartime constitutional continuity.

faq.question: How is Syed Nazrul Islam connected to 1971?
faq.answer: Syed Nazrul Islam is linked to the Liberation War through the project timeline as Acting President of the Provisional Government. He preserved constitutional continuity of the wartime state and stabilized political decision-making during a period of leadership.
